The Care Reassessment Preparation Checklist

What to write down, ask and keep track of while Dad is managing at home.

Download PDF

Dad manages at home with a little help, and nothing has gone wrong. That makes today's picture an easy one to put on paper. Take these in any order, with no date to finish by. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something not yet written down or asked, and that is all it is.

Write down

Ask

Keep track of

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you write down, ask and keep track. It doesn't say which changes matter, whether Dad's help will ever need to change, or what kind of help that would be. A page with every box checked is still a record of today. What a change would mean is for the people who assess him, and for the next step below.

Ready for the next step?

You've put today's help on paper and lined up what to ask. The care interview asks about every area of Dad's daily life, including the ones that are fine right now, so the record isn't assembled from memory, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Create Your Free Family Care Profile ›

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow the questions the Family Caregiver Alliance suggests families answer on paper: what help the person needs now, and what help family members can give. The item marked 2 follows the National Institute on Aging's advice to ask the person directly. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.

  1. Family Caregiver Alliance, Caregiving at Home: A Guide to Community Resources
  2. National Institute on Aging, Does an Older Adult in Your Life Need Help?
